items.title: Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Festival Raises $10 Million for Women and Girls Nonprofits
items.summary:
Olivia Rodrigo announced that the first edition of her Daisy Chain Fields Festival has raised $10 million for nonprofit organizations serving women and girls, with the figure revealed on the eve of the event. All net proceeds from the festival will be distributed across 10 groups.

The beneficiaries span several areas of women's health and economic security. They include Baby2Baby, which distributes diapers, formula, clothing and food to children in need; Black Mamas Matter Alliance, which supports Black mothers before, during and after pregnancy; and the National Women's Law Center. Reproductive rights and health care access organizations make up a large share of the list, among them the Center for Reproductive Rights, Planned Parenthood, Jhpiego, the Johns Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health and the National Institute for Reproductive Health, alongside FreeFrom and the National Domestic Workers Alliance.

In a statement, Rodrigo credited the people who made the total possible. "I'm so grateful to every person who bought a ticket, every artist who waived their fee, every sponsor for signing onto a brand new festival, and every donation that helped get to $10 million dollars to support women and girls," she said, describing the festival as a celebration of "the power of what can happen when we come together to support one another."

At a Friday press conference covered by Rolling Stone, Rodrigo pointed to Lilith Fair as the model for what she built. "Before Lilith Fair, women were told that they couldn't lead a festival, that no one would come, that they couldn't get sponsors, and those women proved everyone wrong," she said. "Thanks to those trailblazers, we are obviously in a very different situation now."

The lineup has Rodrigo headlining, with Bikini Kill, Chappell Roan, Devon Again, Doechii, Garbage, Mitski, Rachel Chinouriri, Santigold and the Breeders also performing. Karen O, Sarah McLachlan and Stevie Nicks appear as special guests. Katseye withdrew recently after one member was injured.

Rodrigo said she phoned each of the artists herself and that all of them agreed to appear with 100% of net proceeds going to the beneficiary organizations. "These women are already doing incredible things, and many of them are on major tours of their own," she said. "Words cannot describe how grateful I am for their time and their passion about this festival."

items.title: ‘Coyote Vs. Acme’ Director Celebrates Film Release, Saying “We Won” & “It’s Proof That Movies Don’t Just Go Away”
items.summary:
Coyote vs. Acme is playing in theaters, and its director, Dave Green, marked the occasion with a statement framing the release as a win for the people who refused to let the film disappear. "COYOTE VS. ACME IS FINALLY, GLORIOUSLY, IN THEATERS NOW. Which means one thing. WE WON," Green wrote on Instagram.

The film's path to release was long and public. Warner Bros. had it dated for July 21, 2023, then moved it out of the way of Barbie. In November of that year the studio shelved the movie entirely and claimed a $30 million tax write-off instead.

Warner Bros. completed the sale of the Looney Tunes live-action hybrid to Ketchup Entertainment in March 2025, and Will Forte recently confirmed an August 28, 2026 release date, according to Deadline. Green thanked the new distributor directly, writing, "Thank you @ketchupentertainment for hearing the audience. We're so grateful that you did."

Green also credited the fans who campaigned for the film alongside the crews who made it. He described the release as "a record of the cast and crew, post, prep, and animation teams who poured so much love and passion into it over years and years," adding that the audience's fight "is the reason this film finally made it to the big screen."

Samy Burch wrote the screenplay, from a story by James Gunn, Jeremy Slater and Burch. The plot follows Wile E. Coyote hiring a billboard attorney to sue the Acme Corporation over its faulty products, with Forte, Lana Condor, John Cena, Luis Guzmán and Kenneth Choi in the cast. Deadline reported the film took $1.7 million in previews.

"This is a celebration, it's proof that movies don't just go away," Green said. "We make work so it can be seen and shared — that's the whole reason we do what we do."

items.title: Gladys Knight Cuts Back on Performing as She Transitions to ‘Next Stage’ of Career and Life
items.summary:
Gladys Knight announced on Instagram Thursday that she will perform less frequently going forward, describing the change as a shift into a new phase of her career. "After much soul searching I've decided that I will be easing into fewer performances while focusing on transitioning into the next stage of my career and life moving forward," the 82-year-old singer said in a statement.

Knight said she plans to spend more time on projects with her husband and with her grandchildren, and she told fans the announcement is not a retirement. "I hope to see your smiling faces out and about and on the road," she wrote. "God bless all of you and hope to see you soon."

The decision follows months of reports about her recent live performances, including her leaning heavily on backup singers, missing cues and appearing disoriented onstage. Billboard reported that at her July 25 show at the Hollywood Bowl, Knight started walking offstage in the middle of "Midnight Train to Georgia" and handed lead vocal parts to her backup singers.

Her husband, William McDowell, told TMZ that Knight still wants to be onstage but that her condition varies. "No one is ever gonna make me say, 'My wife is well,' but all she wants to do is sing," he said, adding that she has not been diagnosed with dementia and that the couple will see a doctor for an evaluation.

Knight's son, Shanga Hankerson, has raised concerns publicly about his mother's health, first in 2016 and again more recently. "I don't want my mom out on tour, on a tour bus, wondering where she's at," he told Good Morning America in 2025. Variety noted that Knight, whose hits include "I Heard It Through the Grapevine" and "Midnight Train to Georgia," had continued to tour regularly until now.

items.title: The Who Rehearsed For Possible Tour With Zak Starkey Following Bitter Split: ‘It Sounded Great’
items.summary:
The Who have rehearsed with drummer Zak Starkey again, roughly a year after a public falling-out in which the band fired him, brought him back three days later, then let him go for good the following month. Roger Daltrey told the audience at a solo show at the Encore Theater in Las Vegas on August 26 that the group had gotten together with Starkey to test the idea of a European leg of their Song Is Over farewell tour. "It sounded great," he said, according to a Las Vegas Review-Journal review of the concert.

Starkey posted an image of that review on Instagram and confirmed the session. "Nice one Rog," he wrote. "Lookin forward to tearin it up with the Who again. The rehearsal was great.. I don't think we've ever rehearsed as tough as that. Usually we drink tea and talk about what time we're going home!" In a statement emailed to Rolling Stone, he added: "We rehearsed for an afternoon and were absolutely on fire. I'm so happy to be back playing the music I love with people I love. It's good to be home."

Daltrey framed the rehearsal as groundwork rather than a booked tour. "We had a rehearsal recently to make sure we can think about doing some shows in Europe because we've still got to say goodbye to them and goodbye to some other countries in the world that we had success," he told the Arizona Republic. "It's not over by any means. It's just that was the last tour of America for the Who."

The band last performed with Starkey on March 30, 2025, at a Teenage Cancer Trust benefit at London's Royal Albert Hall, a show that included the live debut of "The Song Is Over" and was hobbled by technical problems. Starkey has said Daltrey pinned the blame on him unfairly. "He came in four bars early," Starkey said. "He just got lost. He blamed it on the drums being too loud, and then it got made into this huge social media thing."

Starkey said he learned he was out a couple of weeks later, with little explanation, and that he holds no grudges. "It's the Who. Weirder shit than this has gone down," he said. "It's the Who — the maddest band there's ever been."

Scott Devours replaced Starkey in May 2025 and remains Daltrey's solo drummer; he was onstage in Las Vegas when Daltrey mentioned the rehearsal. The Who have not played a show since the American leg of the farewell tour ended in October 2025, and no European dates have been announced.

items.title: Julianna Barwick and Mary Lattimore Share Songs From New Film Score
items.summary:
Julianna Barwick and Mary Lattimore have announced their second collaborative album of the year: a score for Threshold, a documentary about Olympic cross-country skier Jessie Diggins directed by Lars and Torsten Brinkema. The record arrives November 20.

The duo released three tracks alongside the announcement — "Cold Open," "Sick and Tired" and "Gallivare 10km." Pitchfork reported the news and posted the songs.

Threshold follows Tragic Magic, the pair's debut as a duo, which came out in January and was supported by a joint tour. Lattimore described the two projects as inversions of each other in a press release, noting that Tragic Magic was built around a limited set of instruments while the score had no such restrictions.

"While Tragic Magic had constraints of instruments we were able to use, including historic, delicate and mysterious ones, along with those constraints, we had total sonic freedom," Lattimore said. "In the case of Threshold, the sky was the limit with instrumentation and we held an expansive palette, but our music existed within the framework of Jessie's life and the vision of the directors."

She called working on both at once "challenging, mind-expanding, and satisfying, in this year of making music as a duo." The three released tracks are streaming now ahead of the November release.
